correctness.rationale: Both arrows are separately projectivized. The generic integral diagonal cocharacter has distinct weights within each factor, so the fixed points are exactly the coordinate matrix-unit pairs. For X=E_{ji}, Y=E_{ℓk}, vanishing of the two compositions requires ℓ≠i and k≠j, regardless of the rank bounds. All surviving pairs have ranks (1,1), belong to every stated closure, and number a(a−1)b(b−1). Localization of compactly supported Euler characteristic is valid for singular varieties; here projectivity identifies it with ordinary Euler characteristic. An independent calculation stratifies by positive ranks (p,q): choose im Y⊆ker X in C^a and im X⊆ker Y in C^b, then choose the two quotient-to-image isomorphisms modulo their individual scalars. These are Zariski-locally trivial PGL_p×PGL_q bundles over products of partial flag varieties. PGL_d has zero compactly supported Euler characteristic for d>1 by free left multiplication by a one-dimensional subtorus, so only (1,1) contributes. The Euler number of the line-in-hyperplane flag variety in dimension d≥2 is d(d−1) by projection to the space of lines. This gives the same Euler number for each rank bound and the full space. The a=1 space is empty since a nonzero X from a one-dimensional space is injective, so XY=0 would force Y=0. The ambient Euler number is (ab)², giving the stated ratio. value.rationale: Biprojectivization is the natural compact parameter space of pairs of nonzero arrows up to independent scalars. The equality across geometrically different component closures and their union identifies precisely what ordinary Euler characteristic cannot distinguish, and localizes the entire invariant to the minimal positive rank stratum. The quotient and cyclic incidence count are essential; this is not an affine component count or a numerical substitution into a chain formula.
